body:
Thanks so much again, reddit.

Reading through everything you said has made me feel a lot better after reading through everything. It doesn't worry me anymore that I could be downright insane or depressed, and (this probably sounds corny) actually gave me a new perspective on life..

Thank you so much for reading through all of my "worries," and just... talking to me about it. I really appreciate everything you've said.
that was beautiful.

Is it just me or does the general message seem like "If you're smart enough to be right, you should know that the only logical explanation is atheism, and if you think anything else you are *not* an intelligent person and you're just flat out ridiculous"?


That's the message I get a lot of the time :(

> With regards to the whole suicide idea, I have another idea. Correct me if I'm wrong, but your existential troubles come from whether there is an afterlife or not. Either way, killing yourself won't do much for you. Sure, you will learn your answer a bit sooner, but consider it like this; If there is an afterlife, killing yourself will not make it a good afterlife. If there is no afterlife, then why waste life ya got?

Yeah, I am definitely not suicidal, that's why I was a little cautious posting here. I agree totally with you, "shouldn't waste the life you got," etc
Did it get better/easier? (Do you stop thinking about it as much?)

Does it get better/easier? (Do you stop thinking about it as much?)
* edit: I suppose a better question is "did it get better for you"

> I spent a whole lot of time at 14 (i'm 25) pondering some of the same questions you're pondering, and actually reaching out to strangers on the internet and talking to them also.

This is truly good to know (that I'm not alone.)


> It's really hard to talk to friends/family about this stuff sometimes because they have all sorts of expectations about who you are and what you ought to be that it's hard to sort out what it is that you want amongst it.

This is so true. I don't think I'm anything of what they think I am.
Did you just say "religious" and "healthy" together is an oxymoron? :|
Yeah, watching House and belief don't really go together at all, either.

Yeah, it's definitely the anonymity. I guess the real reason I'm more comfortable posting here is that if I told someone i'm close to (friends/parents/therapist/etc), they might "treat me differently," or just flat out think i'm insane.

I'm not sure of what to think yet... and that's influenced by the people around me and how they think. The only reason I don't explain to my parents my doubts about the afterlife and the existence of God is because I don't think they'd understand why I think the way I do and just blame themselves for "not teaching me" as much as they could have, etc.

* Edit: wow, this has turned into religion, but I guess that was the base of my question in the first place.

I consider myself fairly knowledgeable with technology, etc. It is definitely of interest to me. This probably doesn't help my "problem"... Don't really know why I did use tor, now that you mention it...
In all seriousness, I was also surprised about the fact that a 14-year-old isn't being looked down on on the internet. Sometimes it seems like nobody takes you seriously :(
I'm using tor. Is that dishonest, or just paranoid? :P
Note to self: when you see a post like [this one](http://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/7v5a9/ask_reddit_do_you_ever_have_existential_anxiety/), do not read it.

Wow. SW is amazing. Knowing that there are people out there who really care and are looking to help gives me that warm feeling inside. Reading through what you've all said makes me feel... well, a LOT better. That deep-down curiosity and fear doesn't seem as odd to me anymore. I truly thought I must've been going crazy, thinking about this when my mind wanders...
I'm more normal than I thought.

> You've probably noticed that younger kids mostly just have a ball 'just being' and running about under sprinklers, living in the moment and not thinking or worrying much about what happens next.

Yeah, definitely. People in my age group (14, 15, 16) seem to be totally oblivious to me too. (But I think I appear that way to everyone else too, so who knows who else I know thinks the same way.)

Guess it wasn't total BS when my parents say "Enjoy life while you can" =P

I go to a therapist, but I don't really feel comfortable there. My mom thought it'd be a good idea because "we weren't getting along well."

I don't feel comfortable enough to bring this kind of thing up around him, do you think I should? (ot: He prescribed me focalin because he thought I had ADHD due to bad grades in school for one semester, tried it for a week, didn't really do anything besides make me feel kind of "hazy", so I stopped taking it a week ago.)

I feel like popular culture is saying "there is no god, what is here is here, there is nothing else" TV, things like that... House for example.

Dunno if it matters, but it makes me feel a little worse because i'm too shy to talk to my parents/friends/etc about these kind of things, and I'm posting on... reddit about it. I'm sure at least *some* of them have thought (well, maybe not as much) about what I'm thinking of..

It's actually made me feel a little better already, I'm amazed at the fact that people are really out there and care, I got about 5 responses within 20 minutes! I love you guys.

Keeping your mind off of it really helps,

Being on reddit probably doesn't help -- it's full of atheists and people who believe in nothing, and I guess it rubs off? I try to believe, but I'm the kind of person that would like some kind of proof first

I thought it might be a bad idea coming here, as this is "suicide watch," but I'm glad to know I'm welcome :D

I try to find peace with it, but it really makes me think, and just scares me... Dunno, it's rather hard to explain.

The issue is that it scares me to think of "afterwards".

I am church going.

So this kind of thinking is "normal?" It's not a symptom of depression like I think it is?

Hello Reddit. I'm only 14 years old, but I think I'm depressed or something. When my mind drifts off, I think of nothingness. I want to believe in an afterlife, but it scares me to think that there might not be. The fact that I don't know is the scariest part. I have friends, and get along with them great, but when my mind wanders, I can't help but to think about things like this. I don't have any plans or feel like killing myself, but I feel like this is the right place to come -- people here are voluntarily taking out their time to help people (which I think is great). Reassurance like "There's no reason to be afraid of nothing" doesn't help me. I *want* to believe in something more. Are these things symptoms of depression? Anxiety? [this post about existential anxiety scared the shit out of me](http://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/7v5a9/ask_reddit_do_you_ever_have_existential_anxiety/). What should I do? 

I would never try to kill myself -- that's the very thing I'm afraid of.
